To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ratio of the 5-HT2 receptor to the 5-HT1 receptor is greater in large cranial arteries and smaller in smaller arteries, that this gradient is stable and resistant to maturation and hypoxia, and that the changes in reactivity to 4-aminopyridine associated with maturation and hypoxic acclimatization may involve changes in receptor density and/ or coupling efficiency for 4-AP in ovine cranical arteries.

the 5-HT receptor types in the ovine cranial circulation are differentially distributed among the three types of arteries and that the ratio of receptor types is not changed by maturation or chronic hypoxia.
5-HT2A receptor-mediated contractions predominate in the Com and decrease in the Main and 2BR, while 5-HT1B receptor-mediated contractions increase in the Main and decrease in the 2 BR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of maturing and acclimatization on the reactivity of the ovine cerebral vascular bed to 5-HT, an important vasoconstrictor.
the mechanisms that underlie the development and maintenance of cerebral vascular reactivity in the fetus, the newborn, and the adult.
the effects of chronic hypoxia and of fetal maturation on the development of cerebrovascular reactivities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relative abundance of 5-HT receptors of different subtypes varies in the different size arteries of the ovine brain and this variation appears stable during maturation and chronic high altitude hypoxia.
the relative 5-HT2 receptor density is greater in Com than in Main or 2BR segments.
5-HT2A receptors are present in the Com and Main, whereas 5-HT1B/D receptors predominate in the 2nd and 3rd order middle cerebral branches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HT2 receptor is the predominant receptor type in the larger cranial arteries, whereas the 5-HT1B receptor is the predominant one in the smaller arteries.
5-HT2 receptors predominate in the Com arteries and 5-HT1 in the 2 BR arteries, and this pattern appears to be stable during maturation and acclimatization.

5-HT1B/1D receptors mediate contraction in ovine craniovascular segments, but that the 5-HT2 receptor is the predominant receptor subtype mediating vasoconstriction in the ovine common carotid artery and is present at lower levels in the ovine main branch middle cerebral artery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of serotonin 5-HT2 receptor to serotonin 5-HT1 receptor is greatest in the common carotid artery, and decreases progressively in the main branch and second branch middle cerebrial artery.

the ratio of the number of 5-HT1 to 5-HT2 receptors in ovine craniovascular arteries varies among arteries of different sizes and types and is relatively resistant to changes in oxygenation and maturation, but the number of 1 receptors may increase during maturation.
the relative abundance of different 5-HT receptors in different types of cranial vessels is not altered during maturation or by chronic hypoxia.
